requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`. I reviewed the three marked tests. I also read `fn[content_end]` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/mod.rs`, which implements the trailing-comment trimming.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Block mapping entries are `pair` nodes named by the written key.** `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` in `src/outline/tests.rs` parses a YAML document with a plain key (`pair[a]`) and a quoted key (`pair["b"]`). The summary assertions check that the quoted key keeps its written form. The same test checks nested block pairs (`pair["b"]/pair[c]`, `pair["b"]/pair[e]`).
- **Flow mapping entries are `pair` nodes.** The same test has `c: {d: 1}` and asserts `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d] 4-4`.
- **Block sequence entries are anonymous `item` nodes.** The test asserts `item@` twice under `pair[e]`. The `summary` helper replaces the 12-hex hash with `@`, so the segment shape `kind@hash` is checked. One item is a scalar (`- 2`) and the other holds a mapping (`- f: 1`).
- **Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.** The assertions check the full selector paths. They cover a pair under a pair, a pair under a flow pair, an item under a pair, and a pair under an item. They also check the line spans (for example `3-7` and `6-6`).
- **Selected source ends at the last non-comment token.** `yaml_selection_ends_before_trailing_comment_tokens` in `tests/outline_content.rs` parses `key: value # trailing comment`. It asserts that the selected text is `key: value` and that the span is `0..10`. `content_end` is a single generic routine, so that one case exercises the whole trimming path.
- **Comment ownership.** This is delegated to the cited `requirements.references.outline_comments`. `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one` also exercises it in YAML: the comment owner is `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`. The leading `# c` comment in the first test is attributed to `pair[a]` (span `1-2`).
- **Selector rules.** Percent-encoding, anonymous hashes and duplicate suffixes belong to the cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, which has its own review. The test here shows the anonymous `item@hash` form in YAML.

**Residual observations (not gaps)**

- Trailing-comment trimming is tested only for a same-line comment after a scalar. A standalone comment line after a nested block's last entry is not tested for the selected text. The trimming is one generic recursive function, so this is not a separate input class that the requirement names.
- Single-quoted keys and flow sequences are not tested. The requirement does not name them, and it only lists block sequence entries as `item`.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
Selected source ends at the last non-comment token. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
